implementation_notes: In TypeScript the identity field is declared by decorator or schema and filled by the ORM: TypeORM's @PrimaryGeneratedColumn() creates an int key with auto-increment/serial/sequence/identity depending on the driver and writes the value back on save, @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') makes the ORM generate the key before the insert (the application-generator strategy), and plain @PrimaryColumn() is used when the application assigns the value itself. Prisma expresses the same three choices in the schema (@id @default(autoincrement()/uuid()/cuid())) and exposes it typed through the generated client. The classic key-generator object is replaced by those decorators and defaults plus the driver.
pitfalls: TypeORM maps bigint columns to string and warns that bigint does not fit number: declare the key as string instead of number, or precision above 2^53 is lost.
repo.save() with an id already present performs an UPDATE after looking that id up, so a stray id in a DTO updates an existing row instead of inserting.
Decorator metadata is erased under isolatedModules or some bundlers unless the plugin is configured, leaving the reflected column type as any; keep the key type in the entity declaration explicit.
